It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one: it is taken only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or when its verdict is stronger, and it then replaces the stored report whole. Otherwise the first report stands, its reason and lowering included, as [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) sets out.

evidence.snippet: **Each round re-derives the inheritance.** After verification and before adjudication, one commit replaces the revision's whole set of inheritances and proposals, built from that round's stored judgements. So a `different` answer revokes an earlier inheritance, and so does a `verifierVersion` bump, whose new records start empty. An inheritance also lapses on read when its root reopens or its dismissal is replaced by any other, even one made at the same time. An identical repeat writes nothing, so the inheritance stands. The verifier judges the dismissal it was shown, so a link records only while the root's dismissal is that one: a replacement made while the verifier runs creates no link.

verification.reason: The trace holds in code. `upsertVerification` (findings.ts 1069-1070) throws when `VerificationRecord.refusal` finds an equal or weaker verdict (verification.ts 131-134). For an equal verdict that is always the case. Confirmed is the top verdict, so a later `confirmed` report carrying `matches: {D: "different"}` is refused and writes nothing. The stored `matches[D] = "same"` stays, and `recordInheritances` (findings.ts 1215-1235) reads only that stored value. The result is an `inherited` link, which leaves the blocking set. Base `after()` let the latest report's `matches` replace the stored ones, so a corrected `different` revoked the link. The head removes that route. The new decision names "its sameness answers" as part of the first report that stands, so this was foreseen. But it weighed only the lowering cost. It did not weigh the fail-open dismissal inheritance, which the base dismissal-carries decision says must fail closed, and which a `different` answer is meant to revoke. The scenario is narrow: it needs a verifier that first answers `same`, then corrects itself at the same verdict. The refusal message does tell the verifier its first report stands.
